feature: Customer Portal v2 -- Change Control (/portal-v2/change-control), rebuilt to the standalone Change Control.dc.html module (Part 4), reading the REGISTER, the RECORD and -- as of this pass -- the BRIEFING's own Gantt rows and per-CR cards from real data, plus -- as of the creation-flow wiring pass -- RAISING real change requests. The fix panel (FixPanel.tsx, shared across every pillar drill-down) and the SOP hub's Execute buttons (portal-v2-sop-hub.tsx) now POST to /api/portal/change-control through a shared mapper (ccCreateChangeRequest.ts) instead of running a local setTimeout over a hardcoded CR-2026-0186; both render the REAL pending-approval state the route returns rather than the prototype's fictional 'approved, both signatures in'. apiTests A8/A9 + uiStep CC20d cover that flow end to end. The briefing no longer keys off the design's fixture CC_GANTT/CC_BRIEFS/CC_BRIEF_ORDER code scheme -- ccChangeControlWire.ts's briefFor() synthesizes a live card off a real ChangeRequest's own fields, and a genuinely-empty scoped register renders honestly empty (dataState 'live' with zero rows) instead of masquerading as the fixture register. StatsBand (the six stat cards + expandable preview panel shown on every sub-view) is now live-aware too, as of this pass -- the last seam that read the fixtures unconditionally. Covers the five sub-views (briefing / register / catalogue / calendar / review), each on its own linkable URL, plus the per-CR record view and the deep-linkable policy view (ccView === 'settings'). MIXED SOURCES BY DESIGN -- see the notes below: the register, the record and the briefing's CR content are live off /api/portal/change-control; the freeze band's own copy, Microsoft message-center rows, collisions, the off-timeline tray, the catalogue, CAB agenda and notification rules are still the design's fixtures because no table backs them. As of the Git #1215 pass the record's SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES decision also resolves the REAL logged-in identity (was a fictional 'Halden' tenant-name string match) -- SD1-SD5 cover it.
notes: WHAT IS LIVE AND WHAT IS FIXTURE -- this manifest asserts BOTH, and the split is deliberate rather than unfinished. LIVE (apiTests A1 + steps CC8/CC8b/CC8w/CC19/CC20/CC21/CC24/CC25): the REGISTER's rows, the per-CR RECORD, and -- as of the briefing real-data wiring pass -- the BRIEFING's own Gantt rows and per-CR briefing cards all key off GET /api/portal/change-control (real msp_change_requests rows), so their assertions interpolate values EXTRACTED FROM THE REAL RESPONSE rather than naming a fixture string. FIXTURE (every other step): the freeze band's own copy, the Microsoft message-center rows, the collisions block, the off-timeline tray, the catalogue, the CAB agenda and the notification rules have NO backing table -- a grep of lib/db/src/schema/msp.ts finds no catalogue, freeze-window, agenda, notification-rule or message-center table -- so those steps still assert the design's own copy, and that is the honest state of the page rather than a gap in the test.

GIT #1364 -- THREE FICTION-LEAKING SECTIONS ARE NOW HONESTLY GATED ON LIVE: the freeze-calendar sub-view (calendar), the CAB/change-review sub-view (review) and the notification-rules block + policy Active-freeze field (settings) have no backing table, so on a real, scoped/LIVE tenant they render the platform's honest NoScanDataState (#1339) instead of the design's fictional Halden worked example ('ERP go-live freeze', the 'Priya Raman · Dana Whitlock · Marcus Bell' CAB roster, notification rules all to 'Priya Raman'). The shared testbed tenant (shane-mccaw-consulting) resolves as LIVE, so CC35-CC37 (calendar), CC40-CC42 (review) and CC47/CC47b/CC47c (settings) now assert the no-data testIds cc-calendar-no-data / cc-review-no-data / cc-notif-no-data / cc-settings-active-freeze rather than the old fixture strings. In fixture/demo mode (an unscoped tenant, dataState 'fixture') the design's worked example still renders, exactly as the CR register's own fixture fallback does -- the gate is `ctrl.dataState === 'live'`. Building real freeze-window / CAB / notification-rule tables is separate future work.

BRIEFING NOW KEYS OFF REAL CRs, NOT THE FIXTURE CODE SCHEME: CC_GANTT / CC_BRIEFS / CC_BRIEF_ORDER were Records keyed by the design's FIVE FIXTURE CR codes, so pointing the briefing at live rows used to render it empty -- a real code had no geometry and no brief -- and the wiring pass had deliberately left the briefing on the fixture. `ccChangeControlWire.ts`'s new `briefFor()` synthesizes a briefing card straight off a real ChangeRequest's own fields (workload / window / state / submitter / rationale / real audit trail / rollback flag) instead of a hand-authored narrative. The 15-day Gantt grid is the design's own fixed Aug-2026 fixture window with no real geometry a live CR could ever be placed at, so every live CR renders as an honest UNSCHEDULED row carrying its REAL window text (CC8w) rather than a fabricated bar position. `useChangeControl.ts`'s dataState also now treats a genuinely-empty SCOPED register as live-with-zero-rows rather than masquerading it as the fixture register (previously a tenant with truly zero change requests silently showed the design's five fixture CRs with nothing to say otherwise), so the briefing -- like the register -- would show a true empty state (`cc-briefing-empty`) for a tenant with none; not exercised live here because the shared testbed tenant always carries real rows.

STATSBAND NOW LIVE TOO (this pass): the six stat cards + their expandable preview panel, shown on every sub-view, previously read `CC_STAT_SETS` / `CC_CRS` unconditionally -- the one remaining seam the briefing/register passes had left behind. StatsBand now follows the same `ctrl.dataState === 'live'` gate as the briefing (`isLive ? ctrl.crs() : CC_CRS`, `ctrl.statSets()` instead of the fixture `CC_STAT_SETS` literal, and the freeze-collision check off the derived `sets.freeze` list instead of a hardcoded fixture code `CR-0142`). Two card values (`scheduled`, `closed`) and one (`decisions`) now compute their number and sub-line from live rows / the route's own server-computed `stats` (`ctrl.wireStats()`, exposing `nextWindowCount`/`nextWindowLabel`/`snapshotsHeld` -- previously read by nothing) when live, and keep the fixture's exact literal copy otherwise. `incomplete`'s sub-line was already generic and needed no change. The freeze card's OWN value/copy stays fixture (`CC_FREEZE`) always -- freeze windows have no backing table, same as the catalogue/CAB/notification rules noted above -- only whether anything COLLIDES with it is now derived rather than hardcoded to CR-0142. CC13 was rewritten below to assert the panel's still-static explanatory note (unconditional copy) instead of the now-gone fixture row CR-0151, and CC13b proves that fixture row no longer survives.

THE TWO VOCABULARY MISMATCHES these steps guard: the route sends the SERVER's display statuses ('Pending approval') and workloads ('Exchange / mail'), while the page's State and Workload filters offer the MODULE's ('Awaiting approval', 'Exchange Online'). Unmapped, every real row rendered as 'Approved' in green -- a change nobody signed, shown as signed. ccChangeControlWire.ts maps both and ccChangeControlWire.test.ts pins them; CC20b asserts the mapped state reaches the DOM.

ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/change-control[/{view}]. App.tsx declares the '/portal-v2/change-control/:view' param route BEFORE the bare route and both before '/portal-v2/:pillar', so neither is swallowed. The five sub-views are shell nav sub-items (portalV2Nav.ts) at /register /catalogue /calendar /review; 'briefing' is the module root; 'settings' is deep-linkable but intentionally NOT a nav sub-item (Round Two moved the policy UI to the Settings page but kept the deep link the header badge targets).

LOGIN-BLOCK FLAKE (known, benign): on a WebView2 that already holds a portal session, the two input steps against #email / #password fail because the login form never renders -- the goto lands straight on the authenticated app. Everything after the login click still runs green because the session persists. An N-2 / N result whose only two failures are those two input steps is a PASS for this feature; see portal-v2-manifest-login-block-persisted-session-flaky in memory.

textContains reads el.innerText / el.textContent, so every assertion below targets RENDERED text, never an input placeholder or an attribute. Copy is final and reproduced verbatim in the page, so these strings are reliable probes: if a section is not built, its string is absent and the step goes red.

DETERMINISTIC CLICKS ONLY: the register row div carries the onClick that opens the record, the rail buttons carry their own onClick, the freeze toggle and the stat cards / stat-panel items are buttons -- all have a data-testid on the element that actually handles the click. The Gantt row's click lives on an inner button, so the Gantt is asserted by its rendered content rather than clicked; the same CR's full detail is exercised through the register -> record path instead.
ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD -- the same testbed account the other portal manifests drive.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree -- these steps only exercise the rebuilt page once the commit under test is deployed to the dev server.

THE CREATION FLOW WRITES REAL ROWS every run -- THREE of them: A8 (the API-level probe), CF6 (the fix-panel surface), and CF12 (the SOP surface). There is no cleanup step and no delete route -- a raised CR is a permanent record by design -- so each regression run leaves three more rows on the testbed tenant's msp_change_requests, always pending_approval (A8's titled 'Manifest check -- raise a CR from the change-control creation flow', CF6's titled after the sharing-capability finding, CF12's after the runnable SOP). That is expected and harmless (the register simply grows); prune them by hand if the testbed register gets noisy. The entitlement rule (Git #1168) is why there is nothing to gate here: CR creation is ALWAYS real and unconditional regardless of the Change Control add-on, so all three succeed without any entitlement setup.

CF1-CF13 ARE THE ACTUAL WIRING PROOF. A8/A9/CC20d exercise the (pre-existing) endpoint and the (pre-existing) live register; CF1-CF8 drive the FIX PANEL and CF9-CF13 drive the SOP HUB's Execute button through their real click paths on the deployed build, so they are what proves the two frontend surfaces this pass changed actually POST and render the real pending-approval state instead of the old setTimeout/hardcoded-code animation. The CF steps depend on the deployed frontend carrying the wiring commit -- runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, so deploy first.

WHAT THE CREATION FLOW DOES NOT DO: it raises a CR and stops. The route writes pending_approval with no approver and exposes no approve/execute/reject mutation (A7 pins the approve 404), so a raised CR does NOT run against the tenant -- it waits for an approval step that is separate, later work. The UI copy says so honestly; the prototype's 'approved for this window / both approvals are in' was replaced because it described a flow that does not exist yet.

SEPARATION-OF-DUTIES NOW RESOLVES REAL IDENTITY (Git #1215, this pass): the record's 'is the viewer the submitter?' decision used to be `submitter.org.indexOf('Halden') >= 0` -- a match against the design's FICTIONAL customer name, baked into live page logic. For any real tenant a live row carries `submitter.org === 'Raised in the customer portal'`, so that check ALWAYS failed: a portal user was offered 'Sign and schedule' on a change they themselves raised, and the separation-of-duties prose always read the wrong 'Shane McCaw submitted this change' branch. `useChangeControl.viewerIsSubmitter` now resolves it from the real JWT identity (email primary, name secondary) against the submitter recorded by portal-change-control.ts (`requestedBy = req.user.email`). SD1-SD5 pin this: they open the CR A8 raised AS THE TESTBED ACCOUNT ITSELF (createdCrCode), so the viewer genuinely IS the submitter, and assert the record shows the 'came from your side' SoD copy -- a branch the old string match could never have reached for a live row. The unit test useChangeControl.test.ts pins the predicate directly (9 cases incl. the exact old-Halden-org shape that must NOT fire). Like the CC/CF steps, SD1-SD5 assert post-fix behavior, so they only pass once this commit is DEPLOYED (runTest hits the deployed build).

ENTITLEMENT GATE ADDED (Git #1173/#1168, this pass): GET /api/portal/change-control now floors at requireRole('CustomerUser') (was 'Assessment') AND requires an active tenant_add_on_entitlements row for feature_key 'change_control' -- Change Control shipped as a real, separately-priced add-on (4 bracket SKUs, services.slug change-control-micro/smb/midmarket/enterprise) rather than a tier-included feature, per #1168's 'creation unconditional, gate visibility only' rule. A tenant without the entitlement gets 402 ADD_ON_REQUIRED on every GET in this manifest, not 200 -- so A1 onward and every uiStep below now depend on the testbed tenant (customer_id 1) actually holding that entitlement. The same migration that creates the 4 services rows and the tenant_add_on_entitlements table (lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-08-23-change-control-addon-1173.sql) also seeds that testbed row, but IS A MANUAL MIGRATION SHANE MUST RUN HIMSELF (schema change, per CLAUDE.md) -- until he runs it, every apiTest/uiStep below that hits GET /api/portal/change-control will read as a hard failure (relation tenant_add_on_entitlements does not exist -> 500, not 402) rather than a soft one, and that is the expected, honest state of an unmigrated deploy rather than a bug in this pass. POST /api/portal/change-control (A8, CF6, CF12) is UNCHANGED -- still requireRole('Assessment'), still no entitlement check -- because CR creation is the 'unconditional' half of the same rule and was already proven ungated by the note above this one.

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the testbed portal account; extract the bearer.
A1 -- the customer-scoped register endpoint responds 200 with an array of the CALLER'S OWN change requests. This is the endpoint the register reads; nothing else serves it.

A2 -- scoped:true proves the tenant's M365 identifier RESOLVED. The route fails closed to an EMPTY register on a blank identifier, which would otherwise look identical to a tenant that simply has no changes -- this is the step that tells those two apart.
A3 -- extract the FIRST row's code. The route orders by id DESC, so this is the most recently raised change request; CC19 asserts this exact code reaches the register's DOM.

A4 -- extract the FIRST row's title, which CC20 asserts against the register's real rendered text. Interpolating the extracted value is what makes this an integration assertion rather than two independent checks that happen to agree.

A4w -- extract the FIRST row's window text, which CC8w asserts against the briefing's honest UNSCHEDULED label for the same real CR -- the briefing has no real Gantt geometry to place a live row at, so it shows this real text instead of a fabricated bar.

A5 -- the row's stored status is the SERVER's vocabulary. Pinned so the mapping under test has a fixed input: if the route's vocabulary ever changes, this goes red here rather than silently mislabelling a change in the UI.

A6 -- the four stat-card values are computed server-side, not sent as literals. awaitingApproval is asserted as a real number so an absent/renamed field is a failure rather than an undefined that renders blank.

A7 -- NO APPROVAL GATE EXISTS ON THIS ROUTE, and this is the step that keeps it that way. The wiring pass was explicitly scoped to exclude the Dev->Test->Prod two-gate flow; a POST to an approve path must 404 (no such route) rather than quietly approving a change against a live tenant.

A8 -- THE CREATION FLOW: the fix panel and the SOP hub raise a REAL change request through POST /api/portal/change-control. This is that endpoint, driven directly. It answers 201 and returns the code it assigned. risk MUST come back 'High' even though impactedUsersCount is 3 -- the High rating comes entirely from the conditionalAccess target pattern, computed SERVER-SIDE (the client sends no risk), which is exactly the authority the route refuses to accept from the client. Extract the assigned code so CC20d can prove it reaches the register's DOM.
